what: The navigation handler caches every network response as ./index.html without checking r.ok. One online visit to a wrong URL inside the scope (a typo, an old link, /Buffer/foo) replaces the offline copy with the server's 404 page. The next offline launch shows 'File not found' instead of Buffer. The runtime branch for other same-origin GETs also stores non-ok responses.
evidence: Served /home/claude/buffer/pwa on localhost:8811 and registered sw.js by hand (see T29-14). Cache /index.html was 200 and 770 KB. After goto /nope/ (404), the cached /index.html was 404 and 335 bytes. Offline, goto / gave the title 'Error response: Error code 404'. Screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/80312b5f-0e45-5589-b131-fcf824f33899/scratchpad/beta/shots/T29-pwa-offline-after-404.png
fix: In the navigate branch, cache only when r.ok && r.type==='basic' && the response is HTML, and only for the start URL or index.html: fetch(e.request).then(r=>{if(r.ok&&new URL(r.url).pathname.replace(/index\.html$/,'')===new URL(self.registration.scope).pathname){...put}return r;}). Apply the same r.ok check in the runtime branch.

what: The Google Fonts stylesheet is a render-blocking <link rel=stylesheet>. On slow or hanging networks (hospital Wi-Fi, lie-fi), first paint waits as long as fonts.googleapis.com hangs. This goes against 'offline first'. The service worker does not cache the fonts (cross-origin requests return early), so offline the app quietly falls back to system-ui.
evidence: Used Playwright to route fonts.googleapis.com so it hangs for 8 s. first-contentful-paint came at 8092 ms; normally it is about 240–410 ms. Screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/80312b5f-0e45-5589-b131-fcf824f33899/scratchpad/beta/shots/T29-liefi-fonts.png. Offline PWA: computed font-family is 'Atkinson Hyperlegible' but the font was never fetched.
fix: Self-host Atkinson Hyperlegible and JetBrains Mono as woff2 (inline them as data: URIs as the pixel font already is, about 60–90 KB for latin subsets), or load the CSS without blocking (<link rel=preload as=style onload="this.rel='stylesheet'">) and add a fonts cache to sw.js (stale-while-revalidate for fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com).

what: Navigation is network-first with no timeout. On a hanging network the installed app shows nothing until the request fails. That took 10.4 s in the test, and real browsers can take 30 s or more. The cached copy is used only after the network gives up.
evidence: With the SW controlling the page, context.route made the document request hang 10 s. DOMContentLoaded came at 10.4 s.
fix: Use cache-first for navigation, with a background update (stale-while-revalidate): respond with caches.match('./index.html') immediately, and fetch and update the cache in the background (respecting r.ok). Or race the network against a 2–3 s timeout. Bumping V already handles new releases.

what: The five-second drill's setInterval belongs to the old SP object. If you leave mid-item (tab bar, Back) and then start any drill, the orphaned interval keeps running every 50 ms forever. It calls clearInterval(SP.tick) on the new SP and spAnswer(null) on the new drill's items, so every item of the new drill (including Real printouts and Handover) is auto-marked 'Time up' after 5 s and counted wrong. This lasts until reload.
evidence: startSpeed('five'), wait 1 s, go('today'), startSpeed('noisy'), wait 5.5 s: the feedback shows 'Time up.', SP.hist=[false], and 1 live interval. Click Next: item 2 also gets 'Time up' at 5 s. Screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/80312b5f-0e45-5589-b131-fcf824f33899/scratchpad/beta/shots/T29-speed-orphan.png
fix: Capture the drill in the closure: const sp=SP; sp.tick=setInterval(()=>{if(SP!==sp||VIEW!=='speed'){clearInterval(sp.tick);return;}...}). In startSpeed() and in go() when leaving 'speed', also clear SP.tick and SP.hide on the old SP before replacing it.

what: Leaving a five-second item mid-countdown still fires spAnswer(null) 5 s later in the hidden view. It counts a read (S.read++, touchDay, save) and a miss for a gas the user never saw out.
evidence: startSpeed('five'), go('today') after 0.5 s, wait 5.2 s: S.read increments and the day is marked active.
fix: Stop the timer when VIEW!=='speed' (see the fix above). Optionally pause on document.hidden.

what: Restore replaces the whole state in one tap. There is no confirmation, no summary of what will be overwritten, and no undo copy. Any JSON that has a 'done' or 'kinds' key passes the check, so a truncated or partial paste wipes the gas log, lessons and history.
evidence: Loaded a state with 360 gases and 98 lessons done, pasted {"done":{}} and pressed Restore: 'Restored.' Now 0 gases and 0 lessons, and localStorage holds only buffer.v1 with no previous copy.
fix: Before applying, show 'This backup: N lessons, N gases, saved dd/mm/yyyy. Replace this device's progress (N lessons, N gases)?' and require a second tap. Write the current state to buffer.v1.prev first and offer 'Undo restore' for the session. Reject backups that have no v or savedAt, or offer to merge them with the Drive merge function (hub merge/unionArr) instead of replacing.

what: If buffer.v1 fails to parse (truncated write, manual edit, a bad Drive or backup paste), load() silently falls back to defaults. The first save() then overwrites the damaged original, so even partly recoverable data is lost and the user is never told.
evidence: Seeded buffer.v1 with '{"v":4,"done":{"l1":1},"xp":5' (truncated). The app opens as a new user with no message, and after the first save the stored value is the default state. Screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/80312b5f-0e45-5589-b131-fcf824f33899/scratchpad/beta/shots/T29-migr-corrupt.png
fix: In load()'s catch, copy the raw string to 'buffer.v1.corrupt-'+Date.now() (keep only the last one) before anything saves, set a flag, and show a persistent notice on Today: 'Your saved progress could not be read. A copy was kept. Restore from Drive or a backup.' Add a 'Download damaged save' button in Settings.

where: migrate(): array items and nested values not validated
what: migrate() checks only top-level types. Null or wrong-shaped items inside arrays (gaslog, sess, mist, cmist, reflex.hist) and null values inside maps (flash, cases, speed, scen, steps, teach) pass through. They crash Today, Practice, Progress, Flash, Cases and the Gas log, and the crash screen comes back on every launch because the bad data is saved again. Same-type but invalid primitives also pass: units:'furlongs', lvl:99 or 0, sessLen:-5 (a session of -5 gases ends at once at '0/0'), goal:0, patm:0 (A–a uses a barometric pressure of 0), theme:'neon', skin:'blue'. ui.simPace:'fast' freezes the timed sim clock, because tick%'fast' is NaN.
evidence: Seeded state with gaslog:[null,5,{}], sess:[null], flash:{f1:null}, cases:{'ch-dka':null}: CRASH on today, practice, progress, flash, cases and tool-log. Console: "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'd'|'n'|'box'|'del')". reflex.hist:[null] alone crashes practice and progress. Stored state after load still contains the nulls. Screenshots /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/80312b5f-0e45-5589-b131-fcf824f33899/scratchpad/beta/shots/T29-migr-wrongtypes.png, T29-migr-nested.png
fix: Add per-field sanitisers in migrate(): filter arrays to plain objects with the required keys (gaslog: id string and v object; sess: d and m; reflex.hist: numeric l and t; mist: c object); drop map entries that are not objects; clamp enums and ranges (units in mmHg/kPa, lvl 1–4, sessLen and goal from their select options, patm 500–800, agref 4–16, theme and skin enums, ui.simPace integer 1–10); cap days at 400 and remove invalid dates. Add a unit test in tests/ that feeds these shapes and renders every view.

what: S.ui.simPace is read by the sim timer but nothing in the UI sets it, so it is dead config, and a bad value from a synced state stops the sim clock (see above).
evidence: grep: simPace appears only in ui8.js:105.
fix: Either add a pace control (for example Calm 1×, Shift 2×, Resus 3×) that validates to an integer, or remove the lookup and use a constant.

what: Two tabs stay in sync only through the savedAt string comparison. If a tab's S.savedAt is ahead of the clock (adopt() copies savedAt from Drive, which may come from a device whose clock is fast), that tab ignores the other tab's saves and its next save silently overwrites them (last writer wins on the whole state).
evidence: Two pages in one context: normal sync works (gases from A and B both kept, the units change follows). After setting A's S.savedAt to 2099, B adds gas 'fromB3'; A ignores it, A adds 'fromA4', and the stored log ends 'fromA1,fromB1,fromB2,fromA4' because fromB3 is lost.
fix: The value in the storage event is by definition the latest write, so always adopt it, merged with the in-memory state through the existing Drive merge (hub.js merge/unionArr). Or use a monotonic per-save counter (rev) instead of wall-clock savedAt. Do not copy a remote savedAt into local S.savedAt in adopt(); keep it as remoteSavedAt.

what: When localStorage is full, the user gets one 2.6 s toast ('Progress could not be saved in this browser.') and every later save fails silently. Gases added after that toast disappear on reload, and nothing tells the user to make a backup. The 'Saved to the gas log' toast still appears.
evidence: Heavy state (360 gases) plus filler up to the quota of about 5.17 M chars: logAdd twice, SAVE_OK=false, 362 in memory, 360 stored; after reload 360. Screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/80312b5f-0e45-5589-b131-fcf824f33899/scratchpad/beta/shots/T29-quota-full.png
fix: Keep a persistent banner while SAVE_OK is false, with 'Copy backup' and 'Free space' actions (trim deleted gas-log tombstones, old reflex.hist, cmist). Make logAdd report failure ('Not saved: storage full') instead of the success toast. Call navigator.storage.persist() once on the installed PWA.

what: The gas log is the only uncapped store and dominates growth: about 920 bytes per gas with a 420-character note, because label and line (derived interpretation text) are stored with every entry. Deleted entries stay forever as tombstones {id,t,del,u}. Measured: 1 month of heavy use (30 gases, 40 sessions, 40 case mistakes) is 78 KB; 6 months/360 gases is 471 KB (gaslog 331 KB, cmist 67 KB). That is safe for about 5 years at 5 MB but grows without bound, and the Drive state.json grows the same way.
evidence: storage.py fill run: per-entry 921 B; keys ranked gaslog > cmist > reflex > qmiss.
fix: Store only the inputs (v, sample, note, tag, t) and recompute label/line on render (interp is fast). Purge tombstones older than 90 days once Drive has synced them. Show the storage used in Settings.

what: onRz() removes a widget's resize listener only when a resize event fires after the widget is gone. Without resizes (typical on a phone or the Steam Deck), every model, lesson figure and tool mount adds a listener that keeps its detached DOM tree alive.
evidence: Opening all 15 models, 10 tools and views 3 times: window resize listeners went 1→10→19→28; after two passes through all lessons, 58. CDP DOM nodes reached 9034 against 3060 live and fell to 5150 only after a resize.
fix: Keep a registry: const RZ=new Set(); one global resize listener that iterates RZ and deletes disconnected entries. Also sweep RZ in go() after rendering (delete entries whose el is not connected). Or use a ResizeObserver on el, which is collected with the element.

what: The rbc (e2.js:127) and kidney (e3.js:114) animations add a window 'buffer:show' listener on every mount and never remove it, so their closures and detached canvases accumulate.
evidence: Leak run: buffer:show listeners 0→2→4→6 per round of models, and 16 after all lessons twice. They survive resizes, which leaves about 2000 detached DOM nodes kept alive.
fix: Use a named handler and remove it in the frame() branch that finds the canvas disconnected: if(!cv||!cv.isConnected){cancelAnimationFrame(raf);removeEventListener('buffer:show',onShow);return;}. Or keep a single global show bus with a Set as above.

what: Same leak as rbc: the kidney model's 'buffer:show' listener (e3.js:114) is never removed (see the e2.js entry). Listed separately because a second file must change.
evidence: See the leak run above.
fix: Remove the listener when the canvas is disconnected, as for rbc.

what: URL.createObjectURL(file) is never revoked, so each photo read keeps the full camera image (often 3–8 MB) in memory until the page closes.
evidence: Code: ui10.js:16, i.src=u with no URL.revokeObjectURL.
fix: Call URL.revokeObjectURL(u) in img.onload and img.onerror.

what: The OCR cache 'buffer-ocr-1' is not tied to the tesseract version and is never pruned, so bumping OCR_JS leaves old copies (several MB of wasm and traineddata) behind forever. It is also unverified that the tesseract language data and core wasm requested from the blob worker go through this cache (tesseract v5 also keeps its own IndexedDB copy). I could not test this here because cdn.jsdelivr.net is blocked in this sandbox: doubt.
evidence: Code review of sw.js. Offline without a cached reader, loadOCR() rejects with 'could not download the reader' (verified).
fix: Name the cache after the version ('buffer-ocr-5.1.1') and delete other buffer-ocr-* caches in activate. Pin workerPath, corePath and langPath in createWorker to explicit jsDelivr URLs so they match the SW rule. Test once on a real device in airplane mode.

what: SW registration is gated on location.protocol==='https:', so it never registers on http://localhost. Developers and testers cannot check offline behaviour locally, which is how the 404 cache bug above went unnoticed.
evidence: On http://localhost:8811/ isSecureContext=true but registrations=0.
fix: Gate on window.isSecureContext && location.protocol!=='file:' instead.

what: The standalone buffer.html has no <!doctype>, <meta charset> or viewport meta (the PWA index.html has them). Opened directly as a file, it renders in quirks mode at 980 px wide on a phone, and in 1 of about 18 loads it was decoded as windows-1252 (the header streak emoji showed as mojibake 'ð\x9f\x94¥'). This applies only to the downloaded or file copy; the claude.ai wrapper may add the skeleton.
evidence: document.compatMode='BackCompat', innerWidth 980 with is_mobile 390 px; mojibake seen once in the migration run 'corrupt'. Screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/80312b5f-0e45-5589-b131-fcf824f33899/scratchpad/beta/shots/T29-file-mobile.png
fix: Put <meta charset="utf-8"> and <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1,viewport-fit=cover"> at the very top of shell.html (both are harmless inside the artifact wrapper).

where: Settings → Google & Citrus line on file://
what: Opened from a file, Settings says 'You are viewing the claude.ai copy', which is wrong for a downloaded file.
evidence: file:// load, go('settings').
fix: Branch on location.protocol==='file:': 'You opened Buffer as a file. Google sign-in needs the installed copy…'.

what: Reloading during a speed drill lands on '#speed' with an empty page that says 'Pick a drill in Practice.', and the drill is gone.
evidence: startSpeed('noisy'), answer one, reload. Screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/80312b5f-0e45-5589-b131-fcf824f33899/scratchpad/beta/shots/T29-reload-midspeed.png
fix: In route(), redirect '#speed' with SP=null to practice, or store {mode,i,ok} in sessionStorage and offer 'Resume drill'.

where: reload mid timed sim / mid chat case
what: Reload restarts a timed sim at 00:00 and a chat case at step 1 without saying so; wrong turns already logged stay in the notebook. This is acceptable, but the user is not told.
evidence: openCase('sim-sepsis'), wait 6 s, act, reload: CS.t goes 3→0. Chat case ch-dka also restarts at 1/4.
fix: Keep CS (minus Sets) in sessionStorage and offer 'Resume where you were' or 'Start again'.

where: gas log sheet: reload with a typed note
what: Reloading or switching apps with the 'Save to gas log' sheet open loses the typed note and tag (the roadmap says the log is kept as typed).
evidence: saveSheet() open, fill #lgNote, reload: the sheet is gone and nothing is kept.
fix: Keep an unsent draft in sessionStorage (per viewer) and restore it the next time the sheet opens for the same gas.

what: Bundle: 779 KB raw, 270 KB gzip. Content files c1–c12 are 312 KB (40%), UI 300 KB, engine 98 KB, CSS 59 KB, and the embedded font only 4.9 KB. Load is about 240–460 ms to FCP on this 2-CPU machine, the heap is about 3–4 MB, and Learn renders in 9 ms. Performance is fine; the content will keep growing.
evidence: perf.py, 4 runs per viewport.
fix: No action needed now. If content passes about 1.5 MB, move lesson bodies into a JSON <script type=application/json> block parsed on first open of Learn.

what: Add a debug 'Check my data' action in Settings that runs the sanitiser, reports what was fixed, and shows the storage used by area (gas log, mistakes, history).
evidence: Follows from the migration findings.
fix: A Settings row that calls sanitize(S) and lists the counts.

what: With skipWaiting and clients.claim, a new version takes over mid-session. Show an 'Updated to 4.x, reload when ready' toast on the controllerchange event instead of switching silently.
evidence: Code review.
fix: navigator.serviceWorker.addEventListener('controllerchange',()=>toast('Buffer updated. Reload when you finish this gas.'))

what: Mid-session reload (or the OS killing the PWA) drops the session silently. Persist SS minimally (mode, items, index, answers) in sessionStorage and offer to resume.
evidence: Reload mid-session lands on Practice with nothing recorded for the partial session.
fix: Write SS on each answer and add a resume card on Practice/Today.
